newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya, Morocco sign deal to manufacture Fiat cars.
newsitem.headline: Libya, Morocco sign deal to manufacture Fiat cars.

text.p: The Libyan and Moroccan governments have signed a deal to manufacture Fiat cars, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Friday.
JANA, monitored in Tunis, said the agreement was signed at the coastal Libyan city of Sirt at the end of a three-day visit to Libya by Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali.
"The agreement is for establishing joint projects for manufacturing cars in the two countries to reinforce and boost their bilateral cooperation in all domains," JANA said.
Two Fiat cars of the model to be manufactured had been offered to Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi by the Moroccan business delegation accompagning Filali on his visit, JANA said.
Libya and Morocco would provide 60 percent of the car's components and the Libyan input would be from the iron and steel mill at Misrata and from the country's petrochemical complex, it added.

"The establishment of a car plant by Libya and Morocco will be a great step in the right direction for cooperation between the two countries particularly as the production of components will be 60 percent of Maghreb origin at the start and 80 percent a few years later," Gaddafi told the Moroccan delegation he received on Thursday.
The agreement was signed by Libyan Industry and Mining Minister Muftah Azzouz and Moroccan Trade, Industry and Handicrafts Minister Driss Jettou.
Libya and Morocco are members along with Tunisia, Algeria and Mauritania of the Arab Maghreb Union established in 1989 with the aim of establishing an economic grouping.

In Turin, a Fiat spokesman told Reuters: "Fiat Auto is fully aware of the deal reached by the Moroccan and Libyan governments. This should be seen in the framework of a further expansion of the Moroccan auto industry in which Fiat plays a significant part. It is a step also towards strengthening trade agreements among Maghreb countries".

The spokesman said Somaca, a joint venture between the Moroccan government and Fiat, assembled the Uno model and would start production next year of the Palio "world car" at an existing plant near Casablanca.
The spokesman made no mention of any new plant being established for the purpose of the project, either in Morocco or in Libya.
